apollo.title: Apollo 11 · What stayed on the Moon?
apollo.question: The astronauts came home. Which objects kept their story on the Moon?

goals.title: Follow Eagle home
goals.objective: Compare the landing stage and the crew cabin.
goals.prompt: Which part stayed on the Moon?
choices: The crew cabin with the astronauts
goals.explanation: The lower stage stayed behind and served as the launch platform. The upper stage carried the astronauts back to lunar orbit.
goals.hint: Look for the lower stage and landing legs.
goals.takeaway: Eagle’s lower stage stayed; its upper stage lifted off.

goals.title: Send a light pulse
goals.objective: Use the science screen to follow light from Earth to the reflector.
goals.prompt: Where is the laser that starts this measurement?
goals.explanation: An Earth-based laser sends light to a passive reflector. The reflector does not need a radio transmitter to return that light.
goals.hint: Follow the light path from its starting point.
goals.takeaway: The lunar reflector returns light sent from Earth.

goals.title: Bring evidence to a laboratory
goals.prompt: Which evidence could scientists study in laboratories on Earth?
goals.explanation: Returned rock and soil samples are physical evidence that laboratories can study. A story illustration is not a lunar sample.
goals.hint: Compare an original sample with an imagined illustration.
goals.takeaway: Returned lunar samples let laboratories investigate real material.

viking.title: Viking 1 · What counts as evidence?
viking.question: Can one exciting signal answer every scientific question?

goals.title: Read a real Mars measurement
goals.objective: Open Science Data and compare the first and last displayed sols.
goals.prompt: Which displayed day has the higher daily mean pressure?
goals.explanation: The recorded mean is 7.629 mbar on Sol 1 and 7.286 mbar on Sol 30. This compares two archived observations, not live weather or a prediction.
goals.hint: Compare the two recorded numbers; do not guess the trend beyond this archive.
goals.takeaway: I can compare two original NASA PDS pressure measurements.

goals.title: Question an exciting result
goals.objective: Read what Viking’s soil experiments could and could not establish.
goals.prompt: What is supported by these results?
choices: Puzzling chemistry, without clear proof of living microorganisms
goals.explanation: The experiments revealed puzzling chemistry but did not provide clear evidence of living microorganisms. An interesting signal calls for careful investigation.
goals.hint: A signal and a proven explanation are different things.
goals.takeaway: Interesting chemistry did not establish clear proof of life.

goals.title: Look closely at the first photograph
goals.objective: Open the first surface view and find the lander footpad.
goals.prompt: What kind of evidence is the first black-and-white surface view?
goals.explanation: It is an original NASA mission photograph. The archive preserves its source and credit, while the drawn room is an illustration.
goals.hint: Read the photograph’s image identifier and source caption.
goals.takeaway: Original mission photographs and AI illustrations serve different purposes.

sojourner.title: Sojourner · How does a small rover explore?
sojourner.question: Six wheels, a solar panel and a teammate: what does each contribute?

goals.title: Match a part to its job
goals.objective: Turn the educational rover model and select its solar array.
goals.explanation: Sojourner’s solar array helped provide power. Its wheels helped it travel, while its instruments investigated the surroundings.
goals.hint: Choose Solar array in Explore the parts.
goals.takeaway: Different rover parts perform different jobs; the solar array helps provide power.

goals.title: Meet the rover’s teammate
goals.objective: Compare the Sojourner rover and Pathfinder lander models.
goals.prompt: How did the rover’s discoveries reach Earth?
choices: Through the Pathfinder lander’s communications link
By carrying postcards back to Earth
goals.explanation: The rover and lander worked as a team. Pathfinder supported communications between Sojourner and Earth.
goals.hint: The rover explored nearby; the lander supported the link home.
goals.takeaway: Sojourner explored nearby and Pathfinder supported communication with Earth.

goals.title: Compare a plan with the reported result
goals.objective: Use Beyond the Plan to compare the two mission-summary bars.
goals.prompt: What do 7 and 83 compare in this chart?
goals.explanation: This chart compares seven planned days with 83 days reported by the NASA source. These are mission-summary durations, not a series of daily measurements.
goals.hint: Read the unit and both bar labels.
goals.takeaway: A mission-summary comparison is different from a measured time-series graph.

apollo.instruction: Use the labels to compare the two stages. These guided views explain functions; they are not engineering measurements.

parts.title: Upper stage
parts.text: The upper stage carried the astronauts back to lunar orbit. It separated from the lower landing stage.

parts.title: Lower landing stage
parts.text: The lower stage and landing legs stayed on the Moon. The stage served as the launch platform.

viking.instruction: Use the labels to connect hardware with a job. Explore real surface photographs and the weather archive for the scientific evidence.

parts.title: Communication
parts.text: Viking’s radio system sent mission information to Earth. Antennas are part of that communication system.

parts.title: Landing legs
parts.text: Three landing legs supported the lander on the surface. Viking was a stationary lander, not a wheeled rover.

sojourner.instruction: Tap the rover’s wheels, solar array or APXS instrument in the 3D view, or use the matching buttons. The geometry is an educational reconstruction.

parts.title: Wheels
parts.text: Six wheels helped Sojourner move across rocky ground. The suspension helped it travel over uneven terrain.

parts.title: Solar array
parts.text: The solar array helped supply electrical power. It is different from the wheels and the rock-analysis instrument.

parts.title: APXS instrument
parts.text: This instrument examined the chemical composition of rocks and soil. It is shown in a simplified form at the rover’s rear.

pathfinder.instruction: Tap a solar petal, camera mast or antenna, or use the buttons. Pathfinder is the stationary lander in this educational reconstruction.

parts.title: Solar petals
parts.text: The open lander has three petal-shaped panels. Solar cells helped provide electrical power.

parts.title: Lander camera
parts.text: The lander’s camera photographed the landing site and rover. A lander photograph is different from a picture taken by the rover’s own cameras.

parts.title: Communications
parts.text: The lander supported the communication link between the little rover and Earth. Both spacecraft had different jobs.
